description.purpose: The rule set and the arrival ledger of the firewall, as rows: 'rules' says who may speak and what may not be said, 'arrivals' is the stamped trace the rate window counts. Both are ordinary tables -- the whole point of the hive is that the policy is editable with an insert and an update, never with a code change.
description.use_when: One per firewall hive. The screen reads and writes here and nowhere else; a code cell owns no state, so all of it lives in this store. An operator (or a mutation) edits the rules table live -- the screen reloads it on every single turn.
description.not_in_scope: No turn content and no verdict history: what was rejected and why is a hop on the reject lane, and where that gets logged is the parent tree's business. No regex, no scoring, no model: a rule is a literal plus a match mode. No pruning of the arrivals table -- it is append-only and grows; trimming it is an operator's delete, not a rule.
description.emits_meaning: messages[]: one tool_result per op. hop.operation drives the phase dispatch in the screen; the row array of a select IS the rule set (or the arrival window) of that turn.
description.consumes_meaning: messages[]: tool_call turns with store-native args. Which pass a reply belongs to is carried by context.store_origin ('firewall'), the step by context.fw_phase, both promoted by the edge that sent the op.
examples: {operation: select, table: rules, columns: [rule_id, kind, field, value, action], where: {enabled: 1}, order_by: [{col: 'rule_id', dir: 'asc'}]} -> the rule set of this turn, in a stable order
{operation: select, table: arrivals, columns: [recorded_at], where: {channel: 'tg:42', recorded_at: {gte: '<cutoff>'}}, limit: 31} -> the bounded read that decides the rate limit
{operation: insert, table: arrivals, row: {channel: 'tg:42', recorded_at: '<now>'}} -> the passed turn books its slot
{operation: update, table: rules, set: {enabled: 1}, where: {rule_id: 'example-block-injection'}} -> a hot policy change, no restart, no code
